concerns.text: US-1 scenario 2 requires 'total memory usage remains below 4 GB', while FR-006, FR-009, the Edge Cases section, and SC-003 all set the limit at 7 GB. Two different memory budgets for the same redshift-binning step are mutually incompatible; pick one (7 GB appears to be the project-wide constraint).

FR-002 specifies the top-hat filter 'radius of a moderate angular scale', the Assumptions fix it at '5° radius', and FR-005/US-3 sweep 3°–7°. The baseline radius is named three inconsistent ways; state the baseline (e.g., 5°) explicitly in FR-002 to match the Assumptions.

FR-010 mandates 'per-redshift-bin correlation amplitudes and their Monte-Carlo p-values', while the final Assumption states multiplicity is addressed by the global rank test 'rather than individual bin tests'. Reporting per-bin p-values (FR-010/SC-005) while disclaiming individual bin tests is contradictory; clarify that per-bin p-values are reported descriptively with inference drawn only from the global test.
FR IDs jump from FR-012 to FR-016; FR-013–FR-015 do not exist. No cross-references dangle, but the gap suggests deleted requirements; renumber or confirm the gap is intentional.

FR-002 specifies the top-hat filter as 'radius of a moderate angular scale' — this is not verifiable as written. The Assumptions section fixes 5° and FR-005 sweeps 3°–7°, so state the baseline radius (5°) explicitly in FR-002 or reference FR-005's sweep as the parameterization.

SC-004 says alignment strength is 'measured against the theoretical ISW cross-correlation curve' but names no comparison procedure (e.g., χ² or residual difference between observed ξ(θ) and the FR-012 curve over θ ∈ [0°,10°]). Add the observable comparison so met/not-met is decidable.

FR-012 requires computing the theoretical ISW curve 'using the linear-theory model of Granett et al. 2008' but does not name the model inputs (void profile, bias, redshift bins) or the output form (curve over the same θ grid as FR-003). Without this, an implementer cannot know when the theoretical curve is correctly computed; specify the output grid and that inputs match the FR-003 redshift bins.

The idea's methodology sketch explicitly requires 'Apply Kolmogorov-Smirnov test to compare observed vs. simulated cross-correlation amplitude distributions.' The spec silently replaces this with a 'Monte-Carlo rank-test p-value' (FR-004, SC-001) with no stated rationale. A rank test is defensible, but the substitution is unacknowledged drift from the specified statistical procedure — either restore the KS comparison or add an assumption noting the deliberate change and why.

FR-012 (theoretical ISW curve per Granett et al. 2008) and SC-004 are additions not present in the idea, which only asks for comparison against Monte-Carlo ΛCDM simulations. This is plausibly implied by the supervoid hypothesis, but it adds a modeling deliverable (linear-theory ISW template) beyond the stated question — add a one-line justification in Assumptions tying it to the research question, or mark it as a stretch goal.

FR-004 runs 'the identical detection-and-cross-correlation pipeline on each (using the real galaxy mask)' — i.e. only the CMB realization varies while the observed galaxy density field is held fixed. The null distribution then omits galaxy-field (shape-noise, cosmic-variance-of-voids) variance, which is a dominant term in CMB×LSS cross-correlations. This biases the null too narrow and inflates significance. The realizations must also randomize/simulate the galaxy field (or an analytic covariance must be justified).

The sensitivity sweep (7 thresholds × 5 radii = 35 correlated tests) reports raw p-values with no multiple-testing treatment. The Assumptions section claims the 'global Monte-Carlo rank test' addresses multiplicity across redshift bins, but says nothing about the threshold/radius grid. Reporting uncorrected p-values across 35 combinations invites inflated Type-I error; specify a correction or designate one pre-registered baseline configuration with the sweep as descriptive-only.

FR-012 calls Granett et al. 2008 a 'linear-theory model' reference. Granett et al. 2008 is an empirical stacked-void ISW measurement whose amplitude is famously ~2–5× the linear-ΛCDM prediction — it is not a theoretical curve. Using it as the theoretical reference for SC-004 mislabels the comparison target and risks a circular/ill-posed validation (comparing an observed correlation to another observation, not to theory). Cite a genuine linear-theory ISW prediction (e.g. from CAMB/CLASS with the same cosmology) as the reference.

With exactly 1000 realizations the minimum attainable rank-test p-value is ~0.001, and the ISW signal at nside=64 with photometric-redshift bins is expected to be weak (S/N ~1–3 in the literature). The spec should acknowledge the power floor: a null result cannot distinguish 'no signal' from 'under-powered', and the constitution-mandated N=1000 fixes this. At minimum SC-001/FR-010 should require reporting the expected signal-to-noise or the detectable effect size, not just the p-value.

'Monte-Carlo rank-test p-value for the observed correlation amplitude' — the scalar 'amplitude' is never defined (peak of ξ(θ)? integral over θ? per-bin?). FR-003 outputs a curve ξ(θ) but FR-004/SC-001 test a scalar; the reduction from curve to test statistic must be specified or the rank test is not well-defined.

FR-012 requires computing the theoretical ISW curve 'using the linear-theory model of Granett et al. 2008' but does not name the model inputs (void profile, bias, redshift bins) or the output form (curve over the same θ grid as FR-003). Without this, an implementer cannot know when the theoretical curve is correctly computed; specify the output grid and that inputs match the FR-003 redshift bins.

responses.response: Unified memory budget to the project‑wide 7 GB limit and updated the conflicting acceptance scenario.
responses.what_changed: US-1 Acceptance Scenario 2 now says “total memory usage remains below 7 GB”; wording in SC-003 clarified to reference 7 GB.

responses.response: Specified the baseline top‑hat filter radius as 5° in FR‑002 to align with Assumptions and FR‑005 sweep.
responses.what_changed: FR-002 revised to include “radius = 5° (baseline)”; Assumptions bullet added confirming 5° baseline.

responses.response: Clarified that per‑redshift‑bin p‑values are reported descriptively while inference relies on the global rank test.
responses.what_changed: Added explanatory bullet in Assumptions and refined FR-010 wording to “report descriptive per‑bin p‑values”.

responses.response: Documented the intentional numbering gap and added a placeholder comment for future requirements.
responses.what_changed: Inserted comment after FR-012: “// FR-013–FR-015 reserved for future requirements; numbering gap intentional”.

responses.response: Made FR‑002 fully testable by stating the concrete baseline radius.
responses.what_changed: Same change as internal_consistency-7fed6ed4 (radius = 5° added to FR-002).

responses.response: Added a concrete χ² comparison procedure to SC‑004 so the success criterion is decidable.
responses.what_changed: SC-004 now specifies computing χ² between observed ξ(θ) and the theoretical ISW curve over θ∈[0°,10°] with 0.5° bins and requiring χ²/ndf ≤ 1.5 (p≥0.05).

responses.response: Provided full specification of inputs and output format for the theoretical ISW curve.
responses.what_changed: FR-012 now lists required inputs (void radius 100 Mpc/h, bias 1.5, redshift bins matching FR‑003) and states the output is a CSV with columns θ, ξ_theory evaluated on the same 0.5° grid as FR‑003.

responses.response: Justified the switch from KS to a Monte‑Carlo rank test in an Assumption.
responses.what_changed: Added Assumption bullet: “We adopt a Monte‑Carlo rank test as a non‑parametric alternative to the Kolmogorov‑Smirnov test; both assess tail‑probability of the observed amplitude.”

responses.response: Added a one‑line justification for the theoretical ISW benchmark.
responses.what_changed: Assumptions now include: “The linear‑theory ISW template (FR‑012) provides a physics‑based benchmark for interpreting any observed alignment, supporting the supervoid hypothesis.”

responses.response: Extended FR‑004 to randomize the galaxy density field for each CMB realization, eliminating the confound.
responses.what_changed: FR-004 now states: generate both a CMB realization and a synthetic galaxy density map (log‑normal, matching observed mask statistics) for each of the 1000 simulations.

responses.response: Implemented multiple‑testing control for the sensitivity sweep via Benjamini‑Hochberg FDR correction and designated a primary configuration.
responses.what_changed: FR-005 now requires reporting FDR‑adjusted q‑values for the 35 parameter combinations and notes that the baseline (5°, –2σ) is the pre‑registered primary analysis.

responses.response: Replaced the Granett et al. 2008 reference with a proper linear‑theory ISW prediction from CAMB/CLASS.
responses.what_changed: FR-012 now cites “CAMB/CLASS linear‑theory ISW prediction (e.g., Cai et al. 2010)” and removes the mis‑characterisation of Granett et al. as a theory model.

responses.response: Added a power‑analysis requirement and expected S/N reporting to SC‑001.
responses.what_changed: SC-001 now includes: “Report the expected signal‑to‑noise ratio (≈1–3) based on ΛCDM forecasts and note the minimum detectable effect size given N=1000 realizations.”

responses.response: Defined the scalar test statistic used in the rank test as the mean ξ(θ) over the interval 0°–10°.
responses.what_changed: FR-004 now specifies that the test statistic is the average of ξ(θ) across θ∈[0°,10°]; SC-001 references this definition when reporting the Monte‑Carlo rank‑test p‑value.

new_concerns.text: Functional Requirements (FR‑001, FR‑002, FR‑003, etc.) reference user‑story identifiers US‑1, US‑2, US‑3, but the specification never defines these IDs. The User Stories are titled “User Story 1”, “User Story 2”, “User Story 3” without corresponding US‑1/2/3 tags, leaving cross‑references dangling and breaking traceability.

FR-004 introduces synthetic galaxy density maps (log‑normal, matching the observed mask statistics) for each ΛCDM CMB realization. The original idea’s methodology sketch only required generating CMB realizations to build a null distribution and did not specify varying the galaxy field. This new step changes the statistical null model without an explicit justification, representing a drift in methodology.

responses.response: Provided concrete details for FR‑012: model inputs, void profile, bias, redshift bins, and exact output grid matching FR‑003.
responses.what_changed: Expanded FR-012 to list input parameters (CMB cosmology from CAMB/CLASS, void profile = compensated top‑hat, galaxy bias = 1.5, redshift bins = same as FR‑003) and to specify the output CSV grid (θ = 0°–10° in 0.5° steps).

new_concerns.text: FR-004 and SC-001 require ≥ 10 000 ΛCDM realizations, while Constitution Principle VI mandates exactly 1 000 realizations. This contradiction makes the required Monte‑Carlo null‑distribution size ambiguous and thus untestable. Align the number of realizations (and any dependent success criteria such as SC-009) to a single, clearly stated value.
